title: Battleships in a Board
summary: Given an m x n matrix board where each cell is either a battleship 'X' or empty '.', return the total number of distinct battleships on the board.
statement: Given an m x n matrix board where each cell is either a battleship 'X' or empty '.', return the total number of distinct battleships on the board. Battleships are placed horizontally or vertically, with at least one empty cell separating them in any direction.
constraints: 1 <= rows, columns <= 200; rectangular board with only "X" and ".".
Each ship is a straight horizontal or vertical run. Different ships never touch by an edge; diagonal contact is allowed.
Follow-up target: one pass, O(1) extra space, without modifying the board.
hints: A valid ship has exactly one topmost/leftmost starting cell.
Count X only when neither its upper neighbor nor its left neighbor is X.
Scan every cell; if occupied and not continued from above or left, increment the count.
The straight, separated-ship guarantee makes local starts sufficient. No flood fill, visited set, or board edits are needed.
editorial: Every horizontal ship has one leftmost cell, and every vertical ship one topmost cell. All other occupied cells have a preceding neighbor on that same ship. Separation prevents another ship from invalidating its start. Diagonal neighbors have no role. The reference meets the optional constant-space, nonmutating one-pass follow-up.

tests.explanation: One single-cell ship starts at [0,0]; one vertical ship occupies the last column. Count ships, not four X cells.
These two single-cell ships touch only diagonally, so they remain separate ships.
